summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for a painful sickle cell crisis affecting her joints, abdomen, and back, following recent chemotherapy and URI symptoms. She was treated with IV hydromorphone for pain and received one unit of packed red blood cells for chemotherapy-induced anemia. Her magnesium levels were repleted due to cisplatin-related hypomagnesemia, and Neupogen was held due to elevated white blood cell count. She transitioned to oral pain medication, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to continue magnesium supplementation, follow up with oncology for blood counts, and manage symptoms with her prescribed medications.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Malignant neoplasm of long bones of lower limb
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
